name: JPMorgan Chase

profile.reading:
The corporate address at 2701 West 160th Avenue in Broomfield, Colorado is recorded here under the operator name JPMorgan Chase, drawn from mapping data rather than from a public disclosure by the company. JPMorgan Chase and Co. is one of the largest financial services firms in the United States, and like most global banks it runs a distributed network of technology and operations campuses well away from its Park Avenue headquarters in New York. Those sites typically combine office space for operations, technology, and customer service staff with on premises data processing infrastructure sized to the campus's needs, but companies in the banking and financial services sector routinely decline to publish floor plans, power capacity, or server counts for any individual site, treating that information as a security and business continuity matter rather than a marketing point.

Broomfield sits along the US 36 technology corridor between Denver and Boulder and has become a magnet for large corporate campuses. The city is home to major facilities for Oracle America, Intermountain Health Care, and BAE Systems, and it serves as headquarters for Crocs, Vail Resorts, and Webroot. A financial company locating back office, technology, or processing operations in this corridor would fit a broader pattern among national employers who have moved support functions out of the highest cost coastal markets while staying within reach of a deep pool of technical talent along the Front Range.

No press release, filing, or page on jpmorganchase.com describing a facility at this Broomfield address was found, and the city's own published material on major local employers does not mention JPMorgan Chase by name. That absence is itself informative. It suggests this location, if active, functions as an internal operations or technology site rather than a public facing branch, event space, or flagship office that the bank would promote. Financial institutions size their internal data halls to the needs of specific business lines, whether trading systems, retail banking platforms, or enterprise IT, and those decisions are almost never disclosed at the building level even when the company is otherwise highly public about its overall technology investment. Readers looking for confirmed capacity, tenancy, or construction details for this specific address will not find them published, and that gap reflects standard practice in the sector rather than any unusual secrecy about this site in particular.

reading: JPMorgan Chase & Co., the publicly traded banking and financial services company listed on the NYSE under ticker JPM and filing with the SEC under CIK 0000019617, operates internal data center infrastructure in the Denver, Colorado metro area, with third-party tracking identifying facilities in Aurora and Broomfield, the latter reported at approximately 20 megawatts of capacity. As with other major financial institutions recorded in this registry, including Barclays, Bloomberg, and Fidelity, JPMorgan's Colorado data centers exist to support the bank's own retail, commercial, and investment banking technology operations rather than functioning as a commercial colocation offering to outside tenants. JPMorgan does not typically break out individual data center locations or specifications in its SEC filings, so facility-level capacity figures in this registry are drawn from third-party data center trackers rather than the company's own disclosures, consistent with the general pattern among large enterprise-captive operators where corporate financial transparency does not extend to site-level infrastructure detail.
